text:
samir: ran a profiling sweep on 8xA100 (2x4 across racks) for the latest kernel-selection change. p50 stable, but p95/p99 for cross-rack jumps ~3x. suspect all-reduce tail + KV cache miss amplification.
marta: can you paste the perf trace/artifacts? are these EFA cross-node runs or colocated NVLink?
samir: cross-rack via EFA; within rack NVLink trunks. attaching flame graphs in thread (uploaded). p99: single-rack 22ms -> cross-rack 68ms. allreduce time spikes aligned with kvcache refill events.
andrew: this smells like PCIe bridge + host->device shuffles when we fall back to PCIe for some ops. kernel selector chose fallback GEMM kernels for the >2048 seq paths — those allocate staging buffers.
priya_g: run results from perf-bot: sample_id=run-2026-03-01, comm_breakdown: allreduce=45% (cross-rack), memcpy-host=18%, compute=30%, idle=7% :eyes: 
perf-bot: quick summary: topology mismatch detected. Suggest testing 'topo-aware-allreduce' mode and 'kv_prefetch=aggressive'. (run /perf/scan for details)
jason: short-term mitigation: lower batch_slice to 96 for cross-node traffic, enable kernel hinting to prefer in-place alu kernels (no staging). also try ring->tree hybrid for >4 nodes.
samir: repro command I used:
```
run_eval --nodes 8 --tp 2 --pp 1 --batch 256 --kernel_hint auto --kv_prefetch=false
```
changing to:
```
--batch 128 --kernel_hint prefer_inplace --kv_prefetch=true --comm_algo hybrid
```
reduced p99 to ~35ms in quick local test.
marta: nice. can we add a canary rollout for kernel selector with topology metadata? e.g., route cross-rack to kernel_v2 and pin intra-rack to kernel_v1 so we don't regress NVLink paths.
andrew: also worth adding NIC-level backpressure monitoring (EFA queue depths) to the runtime telemetry; helps to detect oversubscription from bursty KV cache misses.
priya_g: i'll open a quick RFC for 'topology-aware kernel hints + comm shedding' and include the perf traces. assigning followups: @jason for heuristics, @andrew for telemetry, @samir for repro scripts.
samir: thanks — will attach flamegraphs and a short script in the RFC. :thumbsup:
